subject: NimbleCare deployment: isolation expectations and next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimblecare.io>, Rajiv Kulkarni <rajiv.kulkarni@nimblecare.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + clarifying questions: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (post-demo)

Elena / Rajiv — thanks again for the time today. Short recap from our discovery + a few clarifying questions so we can recommend the right deployment path.

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary concern: PHI/PII isolation for patient data and legal requirement to demonstrably separate customer data from multi-tenant workloads.
- Preference today: lean toward an isolated deployment (either Dedicated capacity with strict tenancy controls, or Private VPC/on-prem). Hosted API perceived as higher risk unless additional controls are applied.
- Technical constraints: expected steady-state throughput ~350 qps (inference), peak bursts to ~900 qps during batch windows; models will be fine-tuned variants with KV cache needs and cold-start sensitivity.
- Compliance asks raised: KMS BYOK, audit log retention 24+ months, SOC2 + auditor evidence, ability to restrict model artifacts from leaving their VPC.

Clarifying questions we promised to confirm:
1) Regulatory boundary: You mentioned certain data elements must never leave your network — does that apply to all inference payloads, or only PHI-labeled requests?
2) On-prem requirement: Is on-prem mandatory for the initial POC, or acceptable as a later stage (we can run Private VPC in your cloud region first)?
3) SLA/uptime expectations: What is procurement’s target RTO/RPO and acceptable latency SLO for 95th/99th percentile?

Requested next steps from our side:
- Karthik will attach a short note on how Redwood handles KV cache residency and options for Private control plane + data plane separation.
- Share a short security appendix (SOC2 summary, KMS integrations, audit log examples). Attached: NimbleCare_Security_Questions.pdf (your questionnaire we filled live).
- Propose a 60-minute architecture workshop next week with your security and network teams to validate control-plane and data-plane requirements.

If you can answer Q1–Q3 in a quick reply, we’ll draft a recommended path (Dedicated vs Private) with high-level cost delta and a proposed MAP.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimblecare.io>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + clarifying questions: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (post-demo)

Rafael — thank you, good summary. A few quick clarifications: 

1) Regulatory boundary: All inference payloads that contain any patient identifier (MRN, SSN, DOB combined with clinical notes) must not leave our VPC. Non-identified logs for telemetry are ok to ship to a vendor telemetry bucket if anonymized.
2) On-prem: Not mandatory for the POC; we prefer Private VPC in our AWS account first (we want to minimize ops friction). On-prem could be considered for production if mandated by an audit.
3) SLA: Procurement is targeting a standard enterprise 99.9% uptime and 200ms p95 latency for single-request inference. For batch windows we can tolerate longer tails but need throughput guarantees.

I'll loop in Rajiv for procurement timeline; tentative go/no-go decision target is end of Q4.

—Elena
Elena Soto | Head of Data Platform | NimbleCare
elena.soto@nimblecare.io
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimblecare.io>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + clarifying questions: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (post-demo)

Elena — quick technical note to address the KV/cache and data residency points you raised. High level: 

- Private VPC (preferred path you indicated) — we support a split control/data plane model. Control plane (management, billing, model catalog) can remain in Redwood-hosted control plane; customer data plane runs in your AWS account inside an isolated cluster (EKS/GKE/EC2 instance fleet). All inference payloads remain in your VPC; we mount KMS (BYOK) and do not persist raw payloads outside S3 paths you control.
- Dedicated capacity (Redwood-managed) — provides isolated GPUs but still runs in Redwood-managed networking; we can provide strict tenancy, encrypted volumes, and dedicated audit streams, but this option may not meet "never leave VPC" contractual language. 
- Hosted API — can be hardened with stricter contractual controls and customer-specific encryption, but still not equivalent to a private data-plane.

Attachments: redwood-private-deployment-overview.pdf (high level architecture diagram + network flow), and a short checklist for the architecture workshop. Also linking our SOC2 summary and sample audit log exports in the drive link Rafael shared.

Notes on performance/cost tradeoffs (ballpark):
- Private VPC (in your AWS region) will incur additional infra egress and management overhead — expect baseline uplift of ~18–28% relative to our Dedicated pricing for the same GPU footprint due to reserved infra and support overhead (detailed quote to follow).
- Dedicated capacity is simpler operationally but may not satisfy the strict VPC residency clause.

I can join the architecture workshop to walk through VPC peering, endpoint placement, KMS flows, and audit log delivery (CloudWatch/S3).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Kulkarni <rajiv.kulkarni@nimblecare.io>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimblecare.io>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + clarifying questions: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (post-demo)

Rafael / Elena — procurement here. Timeline and asks: 
- Target: Decision by EoQ4 (week of 2027-12-13).
- Requirements: We need a draft MSA with VPC residency language and KMS BYOK language to circulate to legal. Can you provide a redline-ready MSA and a short MAP (mutual action plan) showing milestones and owners?
- Attachments you can provide for legal: SOC2 cert page, sample SLA, and a short technical appendix that confirms no egress of PHI from our VPC under the Private deployment.

Please share the MSA draft and MAP by EOD next Tuesday so we can slot it for our legal review.

—Rajiv

1) We will generate a draft MSA with explicit VPC residency language and KMS BYOK clauses and circulate by EOD next Tuesday (2027-09-28).
2) Draft MAP (milestones + owners) attached as a short one-pager in the drive link; will follow up with a DocuSign envelope for a services order SOW when we have scope confirmed.
3) Confirmed: architecture workshop proposed for 2027-09-29 at 11:00 AM PT — invite to follow. Karthik will lead the tech walkthrough.

Attachments sent to drive and DocuSign links provided in the related_links field above. If anything changes on the timeline please flag it here. Looking forward to the workshop.

Best — Rafael
